unit: Ch 12: The Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Introduction, Structure and Applicability of LLP Act, 2008
explain: The Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008 received Presidential assent on 7th January 2009 and came into force on 31st March 2009.
The Act extends to the whole of India and contains 81 sections (section 81 is omitted w.e.f. 1st April 2022) and 4 schedules.
First Schedule covers mutual rights and duties of partners in the absence of a formal LLP agreement.
Second, Third, and Fourth Schedules deal with conversion of a Partnership Firm, Private Company, and Unlisted Public Company into an LLP respectively.
The Indian Partnership Act, 1932 is strictly NOT applicable to LLPs.
topics.example: If two chartered accountants form an LLP in 2024, their internal governance is governed by the LLP Act 2008 and not the Indian Partnership Act 1932.
remember: Enforcement Date: 31st March 2009
Section 81 omitted w.e.f. 1st April 2022
Indian Partnership Act 1932 does not apply to LLPs
mistakes: Assuming the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 applies to LLPs when the LLP agreement is silent.

quiz.q: When did the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008 come into force?
quiz.why: The LLP Act received Presidential assent on 7th Jan 2009 but came into force on 31st March 2009.

quiz.q: Which Schedule of the LLP Act, 2008 deals with the conversion of a Private Company into an LLP?
quiz.why: The Third Schedule deals with the conversion of a private company into an LLP.

topics.title: Meaning and Concept of LLP
explain: LLP is a body corporate formed and incorporated under the LLP Act, 2008.
It is a legal entity separate from its partners, having perpetual succession.
The LLP itself is liable to the full extent of its assets for its obligations.
Partners' personal liability is strictly limited to their agreed capital contribution.
It is called a hybrid vehicle because it combines corporate limited liability with partnership operational flexibility.

flow.title: Hybrid Structure of LLP
steps: LLP liable for full asset extent

topics.example: If ABC LLP suffers a business loss of Rs 50 Lakhs, creditors can claim against ABC LLP's assets, but cannot attach the personal house or bank account of individual partners.
remember: LLP is a separate legal entity from its partners
Partner liability is limited to agreed contribution
mistakes: Thinking that partners are personally liable for the debts of the LLP beyond their agreed contribution.

quiz.q: Why is an LLP called a 'hybrid' business organization?
o: It is managed by both government and private individuals
It combines corporate limited liability with partnership flexibility
It operates both in India and abroad
It functions as a non-profit and commercial entity simultaneously
quiz.why: LLP is a hybrid entity as it merges the corporate feature of limited liability with the flexible internal structure of a partnership.

quiz.q: To what extent is an LLP itself liable for its corporate debts?
o: To the extent of designated partners' personal assets
To the extent of agreed capital contribution only
To the full extent of its assets
quiz.why: Under Section 3, the LLP as a separate legal entity is liable to the full extent of its assets.

topics.title: Key Definitions under the LLP Act
explain: Body Corporate [Sec 2(1)(d)]: Includes Indian LLP, Foreign LLP, Indian Company, and Foreign Company. Excludes Corporation Sole, Co-operative Society, and notified entities.
Business [Sec 2(1)(e)]: Includes every trade, profession, service, and occupation except activities excluded by Central Government notification.
Financial Year [Sec 2(1)(l)]: Period from 1st April to 31st March. If incorporated after 30th September, FY may end on 31st March of the following year (max 18 months).
Foreign LLP [Sec 2(1)(m)]: An LLP formed/registered outside India that establishes a place of business within India.
Small LLP [Sec 2(1)(ta)]: Contribution <= Rs 25 lakh (or prescribed up to Rs 5 crore) AND Turnover <= Rs 40 lakh (or prescribed up to Rs 50 crore).
topics.example: An LLP incorporated on 15th October 2024 can close its first financial year on 31st March 2026 (covering 17.5 months).
remember: First Financial Year max period: 18 months
Small LLP Contribution ceiling: Rs 25 Lakhs (max Rs 5 Crore)
Small LLP Turnover ceiling: Rs 40 Lakhs (max Rs 50 Crore)
Body corporate excludes Corporation Sole and Co-operative Society
mistakes: Including Corporation Sole or Co-operative Societies inside the definition of Body Corporate.

quiz.q: If an LLP is incorporated on 15th October 2024, what is the maximum permissible duration for its first financial year?
quiz.why: For LLPs incorporated after 30th September, the first financial year can extend up to 31st March of the next year, not exceeding 18 months.

quiz.q: What are the statutory threshold limits for Contribution and Turnover for a Small LLP under Section 2(1)(ta)?
o: Contribution <= Rs 10 Lakhs and Turnover <= Rs 20 Lakhs
Contribution <= Rs 25 Lakhs and Turnover <= Rs 40 Lakhs
Contribution <= Rs 50 Lakhs and Turnover <= Rs 1 Crore
Contribution <= Rs 5 Crores and Turnover <= Rs 50 Crores
quiz.why: Section 2(1)(ta) defines Small LLP with contribution not exceeding Rs 25 lakh and turnover not exceeding Rs 40 lakh.

topics.title: Essential Characteristics of LLP
explain: Perpetual Succession: Death, insanity, or insolvency of partners does not affect the existence of the LLP.
Mutual Agency: Every partner is an agent of the LLP alone, NOT an agent of other partners. One partner cannot bind other partners.
LLP Agreement: Mutual rights and duties are governed by an agreement. If absent, First Schedule provisions apply.
Artificial Legal Person: Created by legal process, can own property and sue in its own name, but cannot go to jail or take an oath.
Common Seal: Optional. If used, it must be adopted as per agreement rules.
Business for Profit Only: LLP cannot be formed for charitable or non-economic purposes.

flow.title: Mutual Agency Mechanism in LLP
steps: Partner acts as Agent of LLP
Act DOES NOT bind other partners

topics.example: If Partner A commits a negligent business error without authority, LLP may be bound if within scope, but Partner B's personal assets cannot be touched.
remember: Partner is agent of LLP, NOT of other partners
LLP cannot be formed for charitable purposes
Common seal is optional
mistakes: Believing a partner in an LLP can bind another partner personally, as in a traditional partnership.

quiz.q: In an LLP, a partner acts as an agent of:
o: Both the LLP and other partners
quiz.why: Under Section 26, a partner is the agent of the LLP alone, and not of the other partners.

quiz.q: Can an LLP be formed for charitable or non-profit objectives?
o: Yes, with prior approval of ROC
Yes, if specified in First Schedule
No, LLP must carry on lawful business for profit only
Yes, if it has more than 10 partners
quiz.why: Forming an LLP requires carrying on a lawful business with a view to earn profit.

topics.title: Partners, Minimum Requirements and Designated Partners
topics.section: Section 5, Section 6, Section 7, Section 8, Section 9, Section 10
explain: Eligibility (Sec 5): Any individual or body corporate can be a partner. Disqualified if: unsound mind by court, undischarged insolvent, or applied for insolvency.
Minimum Partners (Sec 6): Minimum 2 partners. If reduced below 2 and business carries on > 6 months, sole partner knowing this becomes personally liable.
Designated Partners (Sec 7): Every LLP must have at least 2 Designated Partners (DPs) who are individuals; at least 1 must be Resident in India (stayed >= 120 days in FY).
If all partners are bodies corporate, nominees of such bodies corporate shall act as DPs.
DP Duties & DPIN (Sec 7 & 8): DPs must obtain DPIN, give prior consent, and file details with ROC within 30 days. DPs are responsible for legal compliances and penalties.

flow.title: Designated Partner (DP) Qualification Flow
steps: At least 2 DPs required per LLP
At least 1 DP must be Resident in India
Must obtain DPIN and file consent in 30 days

topics.example: If an LLP has 3 corporate partners (3 Pvt Ltd companies), 2 individual nominees of any of these companies must be named as Designated Partners.
remember: Min 2 partners; Min 2 Designated Partners (Individuals)
Resident in India threshold: Stayed >= 120 days during FY
Carrying business with 1 partner > 6 months = Unlimited personal liability for sole partner
DP filing with ROC within 30 days of appointment
mistakes: Confusing the resident requirement under LLP Act (120 days in FY) with Income Tax Act rules (182 days).

quiz.q: What is the minimum stay requirement in India during a financial year for a Designated Partner to be considered 'Resident in India' under Section 7?
quiz.why: Under Section 7 explanation, 'resident in India' means staying in India for not less than 120 days during the financial year.

quiz.q: If the number of partners in an LLP drops to 1, after how many months of continued operation does the single partner become personally liable for LLP debts?
quiz.why: Section 6 provides that if business is carried on for more than 6 months with only one partner, that partner becomes personally liable for obligations incurred during that period.

topics.title: Incorporation of LLP
explain: Step 1 - Name Reservation: File e-Form RUN-LLP to check and reserve proposed name.
Step 2 - Incorporation Document (Sec 11): File e-Form FiLLiP with ROC (Central Registration Centre) containing names, address, business, and partner details.
Step 3 - Compliance Statement: Submit a statement by an Advocate/CA/CS/CMA engaged in formation AND by a subscriber, confirming all legal requirements are met.
Step 4 - Certificate of Incorporation (Sec 12): ROC registers documents within 14 days and issues Certificate (conclusive evidence of incorporation).
Step 5 - LLP Agreement: File executed LLP Agreement with ROC within 30 days of incorporation.
Penalty for False Statement (Sec 11(3)): Imprisonment up to 2 years and fine from Rs 10,000 to Rs 5 Lakhs.
topics.example: CA Anuj files Form FiLLiP along with a compliance declaration. Once ROC issues the Certificate of Incorporation on Day 10, the LLP comes into legal existence.
remember: ROC processing time for registration: 14 days
Certificate of Incorporation is conclusive evidence
File LLP Agreement within 30 days of incorporation
False declaration penalty: Imprisonment up to 2 yrs & fine Rs 10k - Rs 5 Lakhs
mistakes: Thinking the LLP agreement must be filed before incorporation; it is executed and filed within 30 days after incorporation.

quiz.q: Within how many days of receiving the incorporation documents must the Registrar issue the Certificate of Incorporation under Section 12?
quiz.why: Section 12(1) specifies that the Registrar shall register incorporation documents and issue a certificate within 14 days.

quiz.q: What is the penalty for making a false declaration in the incorporation statement under Section 11(3)?
o: Imprisonment up to 2 years and fine between Rs 10,000 and Rs 5 Lakhs
Imprisonment up to 5 years and fine up to Rs 1 Lakh
quiz.why: Section 11(3) prescribes imprisonment up to 2 years and a fine from Rs 10,000 to Rs 5 Lakhs for making false statements.

topics.title: Registered Office, Name, Rectification & Publication
topics.section: Section 13, Section 14, Section 15, Section 16, Section 17, Section 19, Section 20, Section 21
explain: Registered Office (Sec 13): Every LLP must have a registered office for serving documents. Notice of change must be filed with ROC. Penalty for default: Rs 500/day (max Rs 50,000).
Effect of Registration (Sec 14): LLP can sue/be sued, acquire/hold property, have common seal, and do legal acts.
Name Requirements (Sec 15): Name must end with 'Limited Liability Partnership' or 'LLP'. Cannot be undesirable or identical/resembling existing LLP/Company/Trademark.
Reservation of Name (Sec 16): Name reserved by ROC remains valid for 3 months from intimation date.
Rectification of Name (Sec 17): Central Government may direct name change within 3 months if identical/resembling. Trademark owner can apply within 3 years of incorporation.
Improper Use of 'LLP' (Sec 20): Carrying business using 'LLP' without registration attracts fine from Rs 50,000 to Rs 5 Lakhs.
Publication (Sec 21): Invoices, letters, and publications must bear name, address, registration number, and statement of limited liability. Fine for non-compliance: Rs 10,000.

flow.title: Name Rectification Procedure under Section 17
steps: Affected entity or Trademark owner applies
CG issues direction to change name
Notify ROC within 15 days of change

topics.example: If Tech-Solutions LLP is registered and later found identical to Tech Solutions Pvt Ltd, CG can order Tech-Solutions LLP to change its name within 3 months.
remember: Name reservation period: 3 months
Rectification compliance period: 3 months from CG direction
Trademark owner application period: Within 3 years of incorporation
Penalty for improper use of 'LLP' word: Rs 50,000 to Rs 5 Lakhs
Penalty for registered office default: Rs 500/day (max Rs 50,000)
mistakes: Assuming trademark owners can apply for LLP name rectification at any time; there is a 3-year limitation period.

quiz.q: For how long is a name reserved by the Registrar under Section 16 valid from the date of intimation?
quiz.why: Under Section 16(2), the Registrar reserves the name for a period of 3 months from the date of intimation.

quiz.q: Within what period must a registered trademark owner file an application for rectification of an identical LLP name under Section 17?
quiz.why: Section 17 proviso states that an application by a registered trademark owner is maintainable within 3 years from incorporation/registration.

topics.title: Partners and Their Relations
explain: Eligibility & Agreement (Sec 22 & 23): Subscribers become partners at incorporation. Rights/duties governed by LLP agreement; if silent, First Schedule applies.
Pre-incorporation Agreements (Sec 23(3)): Valid only if ratified by all partners after incorporation.
Cessation of Partner (Sec 24): A partner may resign by giving >= 30 days written notice. Cessation occurs on death, dissolution, unsound mind, or insolvency.
Former Partner Liability (Sec 24(3)): Former partner is still regarded as partner by third parties unless third party has notice OR notice of cessation is delivered to ROC.
Rights of Outgoing Partner (Sec 24(5)): Entitled to capital contribution actually made + share in accumulated profits (after deducting losses). NO right to interfere in management.

Registration of Changes (Sec 25): Partner must inform LLP of name/address change within 15 days. LLP must file notice with ROC within 30 days of any partner joining, leaving, or changing details. Penalty for default: Rs 10,000.

flow.title: Partner Resignation & Filing Flow
steps: Partner gives 30 days written notice to LLP
Resignation takes effect as per notice
Partner informs address change within 15 days
LLP files Form with ROC within 30 days
Former partner gets capital + profit share

topics.example: Partner Rahul resigns on 1st March. LLP must file notice with ROC by 31st March. If not filed, third parties without notice can still hold Rahul liable as a partner.
remember: Resignation notice period: min 30 days
Partner to LLP notice for address change: 15 days
LLP to ROC notice for partner changes: 30 days
Outgoing partner gets capital + net profit share, but NO management rights
Penalty for Sec 25 non-compliance: Rs 10,000
mistakes: Assuming an outgoing partner retains management rights over the LLP.

quiz.q: In the absence of a specific clause in the LLP agreement, how much advance notice in writing must a partner give to resign from the LLP under Section 24(1)?
quiz.why: Section 24(1) provides that a partner may resign by giving a notice in writing of not less than 30 days to other partners.

quiz.q: Within how many days must an LLP file a notice with the ROC after a person becomes or ceases to be a partner under Section 25(2)?
quiz.why: Section 25(2) mandates filing a notice with the Registrar within 30 days from the date a person becomes or ceases to be a partner.

topics.title: Extent and Limitation of Liability of LLP and Partners
topics.section: Section 26, Section 27, Section 28, Section 29, Section 30, Section 31
explain: Agency & Liability (Sec 26 & 27): Partner is agent of LLP, not of other partners. LLP not bound if partner acted without authority AND 3rd party knew it.
LLP is liable for wrongful acts of partners committed in the ordinary course of business.
Partner Personal Liability (Sec 28): Partners are NOT personally liable for LLP obligations. However, a partner is personally liable for their OWN wrongful acts/omissions.
Holding Out (Sec 29): Any person representing themselves as a partner is liable to credit providers acting on that representation. LLP is liable to the extent of credit received.

Fraudulent Intent (Sec 30): If business is carried out to defraud creditors or for fraud, liability of LLP and guilty partners becomes UNLIMITED. Penalty: Imprisonment up to 5 years and fine Rs 50,000 to Rs 5 Lakhs.
Whistleblowing (Sec 31): Penalty may be reduced/waived if partner/employee provides useful info during investigation. Demotion, harassment, or dismissal prohibited.

flow.title: Fraudulent Conduct Liability Test (Section 30)
steps: Business act carried out by LLP/Partner
Intent to defraud creditors or fraud established
Liability of guilty partners becomes UNLIMITED
Imprisonment up to 5 yrs + Fine Rs 50k to 5L

topics.example: If Partner X takes a loan pretending the LLP is expanding, but uses it for personal gambling with LLP knowledge, both X and LLP face unlimited liability.
remember: Partner liable for own wrongful acts, not for other partners' acts
Fraudulent act = Unlimited personal liability
Penalty for fraud: Imprisonment up to 5 yrs and fine Rs 50,000 to Rs 5 Lakhs
Whistleblower protection prohibits harassment or dismissal
mistakes: Believing that limited liability protects partners even in cases of deliberate fraud.

quiz.q: What happens to the liability of a partner who acts with intent to defraud creditors under Section 30?
o: Becomes unlimited for all debts and liabilities
Transferred entirely to the Designated Partner
quiz.why: Section 30(1) specifies that in case of fraud, the liability of the LLP and guilty partners shall be unlimited for all debts.

quiz.q: What is the maximum imprisonment term for carrying on LLP business with fraudulent intent under Section 30(2)?
quiz.why: Section 30(2) lays down imprisonment for a term which may extend to 5 years along with a fine.

topics.title: Contributions and Financial Disclosures
topics.section: Section 32, Section 33, Section 34, Section 34A, Section 35, Section 36
explain: Form of Contribution (Sec 32 & 33): Contribution may be money, tangible/intangible property, promissory notes, or contracts for services. Must be accounted for in books.
Maintenance of Books (Sec 34(1)): LLP must maintain proper books of account on cash or accrual double-entry basis at registered office for prescribed period.

Statement of Account & Solvency (Sec 34(2) & (3)): Prepared within 6 months from end of FY, signed by DPs, and filed with ROC. Penalty for non-filing: Rs 100/day (max Rs 1 Lakh for LLP, Rs 50,000 for DP).
Audit (Sec 34(4)): Accounts must be audited unless exempted by Central Government rules.
Accounting Standards (Sec 34A): CG may prescribe accounting/auditing standards recommended by ICAI.
Annual Return (Sec 35): File Form 11 with ROC within 60 days of FY closure. Penalty: Rs 100/day (max Rs 1 Lakh for LLP, Rs 50,000 for DP).
Inspection (Sec 36): Incorporation document, partner details, Statement of Solvency, and Annual Return are open for public inspection.

flow.title: Annual Financial Compliance Timeline
steps: File Annual Return (Form 11) within 60 days (by 30th May)
Prepare Statement of Solvency within 6 months (by 30th Sep)
File Statement of Solvency with ROC

topics.example: For FY ending 31st March 2024, Annual Return must be filed by 30th May 2024, and Statement of Account & Solvency by 30th September 2024.
remember: Annual Return filing deadline: Within 60 days of FY closure
Statement of Solvency deadline: Within 6 months of FY closure
Late filing fee: Rs 100/day (max Rs 1 Lakh for LLP, Rs 50k for DP)
Penalty for Sec 34(1,2,4) non-compliance: LLP Rs 25k-5L; DP Rs 10k-1L
mistakes: Confusing the 60-day deadline for Annual Return with the 6-month deadline for Statement of Solvency.

quiz.q: Within how many days from the closure of the financial year must an LLP file its Annual Return with the Registrar under Section 35?
quiz.why: Section 35(1) mandates filing the annual return within 60 days of closure of the financial year.

quiz.q: What is the penalty rate per day for delay in filing the Statement of Account and Solvency under Section 34(5)?
quiz.why: Section 34(5) specifies a penalty of Rs 100 per day for delay subject to a maximum cap.

topics.title: Enforcement, Registrar Powers & Compounding of Offences
explain: Penalty for False Statement (Sec 37): Making false statement or omitting material facts in any document attracts imprisonment up to 2 years and fine from Rs 1 Lakh to Rs 5 Lakhs.
Power of Registrar (Sec 38): ROC can require partners/employees to answer questions or supply information. Non-compliance fine: Rs 2,000 to Rs 25,000.
Compounding of Offences (Sec 39): Regional Director (RD) can compound offences punishable with FINE ONLY. Max compounding fee = max fine for offence.
Second offence within 3 years of compounding CANNOT be compounded (3-year block period).
Enforcement of Duty to File Returns (Sec 41): If default in filing isn't made good within 14 days of ROC notice, NCLT can order compliance.

flow.title: Compounding of Offence Process under Section 39
steps: ROC forwards with comments to Regional Director
RD compounds offence by collecting sum
Intimate ROC within 7 days of order

topics.example: If an LLP fails to file a document and is fined, it can apply to the Regional Director for compounding if the offence is punishable with fine only.
remember: Compounding authority: Regional Director (RD)
Compounding applies ONLY to offences with fine only
3-year restriction: Repeated offence within 3 years cannot be compounded
Sec 41 compliance notice period: 14 days
mistakes: Believing offences involving imprisonment can be compounded by the Regional Director.

quiz.q: Which authority is empowered to compound offences punishable with fine only under Section 39?
quiz.why: Section 39(1) authorizes the Regional Director or officer authorized by CG to compound eligible offences.

quiz.q: Within what period from a previous compounding order is a second similar offence ineligible for compounding under Section 39(2)?
quiz.why: Section 39(2) states compounding does not apply to an offence committed within 3 years from the date a similar offence was previously compounded.

topics.title: Transfer of Interest, Conversion, Foreign LLP & Amalgamation
topics.section: Section 42, Section 55, Section 56, Section 57, Section 58, Section 59, Section 60, Section 61, Section 62
explain: Transferable Interest (Sec 42): Partner's share in profits/losses is transferable. Transfer DOES NOT give transferee management rights or access to accounts.
Conversions (Sec 55-58): Firm (Sch 2), Private Co (Sch 3), Unlisted Public Co (Sch 4) can convert to LLP. Upon registration, all assets/liabilities vest in LLP; old entity is dissolved.
LLP must inform old Registrar of Firms/Companies within 15 days of conversion.
Foreign LLP (Sec 59): CG frames rules for foreign LLPs setting up business in India.
Compromise & Reconstruction (Sec 60-62): Requires 3/4th majority in value of creditors/partners AND NCLT sanction. Order filed with ROC within 30 days.
Crucial Prohibition: An LLP CANNOT be amalgamated with a Company under Section 62.

flow.title: Conversion of Entity into LLP (Section 58)
steps: All assets & liabilities vest in LLP
Old entity dissolved & removed from records

topics.example: If ABC Pvt Ltd converts into ABC LLP, its land and bank balances automatically transfer to ABC LLP without requiring separate transfer deeds.
remember: Transferee of profit rights gets NO management rights
Inform old Registrar within 15 days of conversion
Compromise requires 3/4th majority in value of creditors/partners
An LLP CANNOT amalgamate with a company
mistakes: Assuming a transferee acquiring 50% profit rights gets management or voting rights in the LLP.

quiz.q: Does the transfer of a partner's profit share to a third party entitle the transferee to participate in the management of the LLP under Section 42?
o: No, transfer does not confer management rights
quiz.why: Section 42(3) explicitly states that transfer of profit rights does not entitle the transferee to participate in management.

quiz.q: Within how many days of registration of conversion must an LLP inform the concerned Registrar of Firms or ROC under Section 58(ii)?
quiz.why: Section 58(ii) requires the LLP to inform the concerned Registrar of Firms or ROC about the conversion within 15 days.

topics.title: Winding Up, Dissolution and Miscellaneous Provisions
topics.section: Section 63, Section 64, Section 65, Section 66, Section 67, Section 69, Section 70
explain: Modes of Winding Up (Sec 63): Winding up may be Voluntary OR by the Tribunal (NCLT).

Grounds for Tribunal Winding Up (Sec 64): (a) LLP decides, (b) Partners < 2 for > 6 months, (c) Sovereignty/integrity default, (d) Default in filing Statement of Solvency or Annual Return for 5 consecutive FYs, (e) Just & equitable.
Partner Business Transactions (Sec 66): A partner may lend money to and transact business with the LLP, having the same rights as a non-partner third party.
Application of Companies Act (Sec 67): CG may direct specific provisions of Companies Act 2013 to apply to LLPs by notification.
Additional Fee (Sec 69): Delayed document filings permitted on payment of prescribed additional fee.
Enhanced Punishment (Sec 70): Second or subsequent offences attract TWICE the amount of fine prescribed for the first offence.

flow.title: Grounds for Winding Up by Tribunal (Section 64)
steps: LLP resolves to be wound up by NCLT
Default in filing Solvency/Return for 5 consecutive FYs
NCLT finds it just & equitable to wind up

topics.example: If an LLP fails to file both its Annual Return and Solvency Statement from FY 2019-20 to FY 2023-24 (5 consecutive years), NCLT can order winding up.
remember: Winding up ground: Default in filing Solvency/Return for 5 consecutive FYs
Partner lending money to LLP has status of third-party creditor
Enhanced punishment for 2nd offence: Double the fine amount
mistakes: Thinking that missing annual filings for any 5 years triggers tribunal winding up; it must be 5 CONSECUTIVE financial years.

quiz.q: An LLP may be wound up by the Tribunal if it defaults in filing the Statement of Account and Solvency or Annual Return for how many consecutive financial years under Section 64?
quiz.why: Section 64(d) provides winding up grounds if default in filing solvency or annual return occurs for 5 consecutive financial years.

quiz.q: What is the penalty implication for a second or subsequent offence under Section 70 of the LLP Act?
quiz.why: Section 70 states that for a second or subsequent offence, the fine shall be twice the amount provided for such offence.

topics.title: Differences with Other Forms of Organisation
topics.section: Comparative Analysis (LLP vs Firm vs Company)
explain: LLP vs Partnership Firm: LLP is a body corporate and separate legal entity with perpetual succession; Firm is not. LLP registration is mandatory; Firm registration is voluntary.
LLP partners have limited liability; Firm partners have unlimited liability. LLP requires at least 2 Designated Partners; Firm has no such concept.
LLP vs Limited Liability Company: LLP internal governance is regulated by mutually agreed contract; Company is regulated by statute (Companies Act 2013).
LLP has no upper limit on maximum partners; Private Company is capped at 200 members.
LLP business is managed by partners including DPs; Company affairs are managed by Board of Directors elected by shareholders.
Minor: Minor CANNOT be admitted to LLP; Minor CAN be admitted to benefits of a Partnership Firm.

flow.title: Entity Comparison Key Dimensions
steps: Check Governing Law (LLP Act vs Partnership Act vs Companies Act)
Check Legal Entity & Liability (Limited vs Unlimited)
Check Minor Status (Ineligible vs Admitted to Benefits)

topics.example: A 16-year-old minor can be admitted to the benefits of Sharma & Sons partnership firm, but cannot become a partner or beneficiary in Sharma Tech LLP.
remember: LLP: Mandatory registration, limited liability, min 2 DPs, no max partner cap
Firm: Voluntary registration, unlimited liability, minor can be admitted to benefits
Private Co: Max 200 members, governed by statute, managed by Board of Directors
mistakes: Assuming minors can be admitted to the benefits of an LLP just like in a partnership firm.

quiz.q: Can a minor be admitted to the benefits of an LLP under the LLP Act, 2008?
o: Yes, with consent of all partners
No, a minor cannot be admitted to the benefits of an LLP
Yes, but only for profit sharing up to 10%
quiz.why: Unlike partnership firms under the 1932 Act, minors cannot be admitted to the benefits of an LLP.

quiz.q: What is the maximum limit on the number of partners in an LLP?
quiz.why: The LLP Act 2008 prescribes a minimum of 2 partners, but places no upper limit on the maximum number of partners.
